title: Phenotypic and Genotypic Characterization of Staphylococcus spp. Isolated from Cows with Clinical and Subclinical Mastitis in Kazakhstan
content: Staphylococci are the major pathogens associated with bovine mastitis, and the antimicrobial resistance, biofilm formation, and virulence factors may promote infection persistence. Forty-two Staphylococcus spp. isolates ob-tained from the milk of cows with clinical and subclinical mastitis were analyzed from farms in the Almaty, Zhetysu, and Kyzylorda regions of the Republic of Kazakhstan. The isolates were identified using MALDI-TOF MS, after which their hemolytic and DNase activities, ability to form biofilms, and susceptibility to antimicrobial agents were determined. PCR was used to detect the presence of antibiotic resistance genes (blaZ, mecA, tetM, tetK, ermB, aac(6′)/aph(2″)), as well as genes associated with adhesion and biofilm formation (clfA, icaA, icaD, aap, fnbpA) and virulence (hla, hlb, sea, seb, tst). S. aureus was detected in 17 (40.5%) cases, and S. epidermidis in 12 (28.6%). Bio-film formation was detected in 22 (52.4%) isolates. Resistance to penicillin G and ampicillin was detected in 41 (97.6%) isolates, and the most common genetic determinants were clfA (73.8%), blaZ (47.6%), and mecA (35.7%). Overall, these findings show that resistance- and persistence-related traits are common among Staphylococcus spp. isolates associated with bovine mastitis.
